The test image shows soybean leaves with:
- Yellow-green mottling/blotchiness distributed irregularly across leaves
- Pinkish/reddish-brown spots mixed in with the yellow areas
- Green veins visible with interveinal yellowing
- Upper canopy leaves affected

This pattern strongly suggests a viral disease. The combination of yellow spots along veins progressing to reddish-brown necrotic lesions points toward Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference image for Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus shows early-stage isolated yellow spots with some progressing to brown necrotic centers. 

Comparing to the test image:
- The test image shows more widespread mottling with both yellow AND reddish-pink areas — consistent with SVN at a more advanced stage where yellow spots have progressed to red-brown necrotic lesions
- The pattern has some angular, vein-limited quality
- Randomly distributed irregular yellow areas turning reddish-brown matches the SVN description well

The reddish-pink component rules out Bean Pod Mottle Virus (which is purely green-yellow mottling), and the widespread leaf involvement with vein-limited angular lesions fits Soybean Vein Necrosis Virus best.
